# #46063 - feat(evaluations): add latency and cost schemas

Status at frozen snapshot: merged | Extraction version: 2

## Reusable rules

1. **Prefer neutral names for extensible evaluation models** When a model may later cover more than the current target type, avoid baking “Target” into its model name. The final patch uses names such as LatencySummary and InferenceCostSummary while retaining target as a nested property. *Scope:* Naming shared evaluation latency and cost models that may expand to other model types. *Explicit reviewer guidance.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3926720426, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3928443020, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/6e557e0545a974810613a7f192e691056549ff0a/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/openai/evaluations/models.tsp

2. **Model optional reporting at the appropriate level** Use optional top-level reporting fields when data may be absent, and optional nested attribution when only some categories apply. Here, absent latency or cost is omitted, while target attribution can be absent when another model type supplies the result. *Scope:* Evaluation response schemas whose metrics or attribution depend on runtime usage or model type. *Explicit reviewer guidance.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3968978679, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3969110973, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3969152257, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3970848519, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/6e557e0545a974810613a7f192e691056549ff0a/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/openai/evaluations/models.tsp

3. **Constrain numeric values to their documented domain** Add minimum-value constraints where the domain is known; distinguish values that may be zero from counts that must be positive. The patch uses zero for measurements and costs and one for sample_count. The decimal128 discussion was resolved in favor of float64 to match an existing service cost type, not as a universal precision rule. *Scope:* Numeric fields in these evaluation latency and cost schemas; choose bounds and representation based on domain and service conventions. *Explicit reviewer guidance.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3981034057, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3981421074, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3961331217, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3962441181, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/6e557e0545a974810613a7f192e691056549ff0a/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/openai/evaluations/models.tsp

4. **Keep client-specific decorators in client files, with parameter-level exceptions** The review says client decorators usually belong in the relevant client.tsp. The final patch retains the Java alternateType on the operation parameter because the reviewer explains that this parameter cannot be alternate-typed in client.tsp and prefers the upstream customization there. *Scope:* TypeSpec SDK customizations, particularly Java alternateType mappings on operation parameters. *Explicit reviewer guidance.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3990192593, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46063#discussion_r3991845061, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/6e557e0545a974810613a7f192e691056549ff0a/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/toolboxes/routes.tsp

5. **Preserve discriminator dispatch when substituting Java types** The Java customization comments distinguish standalone models that can reuse openai-java types from models participating in discriminator hierarchies, which remain generated so polymorphic deserialization can dispatch to concrete subtypes. *Scope:* Java alternateType substitutions for OpenAI models used by this Foundry SDK customization. *Inferred lesson.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/6e557e0545a974810613a7f192e691056549ff0a/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/sdk-java-azure-ai-agents/client.tsp

## Caveats

- The optional nested target rationale describes planned applicability to other model types; the frozen patch still defines target as the only nested category.
- The recommendation to put client decorators in client.tsp has a specific operation-parameter exception in the final patch, retained because Java cannot alternate-type that parameter there.
- The float64 choice reflects a referenced service type and does not establish a universal rule against decimal128.
- The description reports regenerating OpenAPI artifacts; generated files were deliberately omitted from evidence. No tests were run. Automated APIView comments are status reports, not substantive reviewer guidance.
